# 1. History of Backpropagation

## 1.1 Timeline of Key Developments

```
1958: Frank Rosenblatt - Perceptron (single neuron, no backprop)
       ↓
1960: Henry J. Kelley - "Gradient Theory of Optimal Flight Paths"
       (Early ideas of backpropagation in control theory)
       ↓
1970: Seppo Linnainmaa - "The Representational Efficiency of
       Tag-Generated Neural Network Systems" (general backpropagation
       via automatic differentiation)
       ↓
1986: Rumelhart, Hinton, Williams - "Learning representations by
       back-propagating errors" (popularized backprop for neural nets)
       ↓
1989: Yann LeCun - "Generalization of backpropagation to handle
       weight sharing" (convolutional networks)
       ↓
2012: AlexNet (Krizhevsky et al.) - Deep learning revolution
       ↓
2012+: Modern era - Adam, modern architectures, massive scale
```

## 1.2 Key Historical Figures

| Year | Researcher(s) | Contribution |
|------|---------------|--------------|
| 1958 | Frank Rosenblatt | Perceptron algorithm |
| 1960 | Henry J. Kelley | Gradient computation in control theory |
| 1970 | Seppo Linnainmaa | General reverse-mode automatic differentiation |
| 1986 | Rumelhart, Hinton, Williams | Backpropagation for neural networks |
| 1989 | Yann LeCun | Backpropagation with weight sharing (CNNs) |
| 1998 | Yann LeCun, Bottou | "Efficient BackProp" - practical guide |

## 1.3 The "Dark Age" (1986-2012)

Despite being invented in 1986, backpropagation faced skepticism:
- **Minsky & Papert (1969)**: Showed perceptrons couldn't learn XOR
- **Training difficulties**: Vanishing gradients in deep networks
- **Compute limitations**: GPUs weren't available
- **Data scarcity**: Limited labeled datasets
